headline: Replit's chief executive says the AI app-building platform has stopped working with Anthropic, but a person familiar with the deal says the partnership is still in place.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by 1: the remark was made on Thursday 15 Oct 2026, before the 16 Oct window, and the claim is disputed.
importance_line: Developers who build apps on Replit may see its AI engine change, and Anthropic could lose a prominent customer to OpenAI, but the claim comes from one executive on stage, an anonymous source disagrees and Replit has not yet answered TechCrunch.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Amjad Masad, chief executive and co-founder of Replit, a platform where people build and run apps in a web browser, said on stage at TechCrunch Disrupt on Thursday 15 Oct 2026 that Replit no longer works with Anthropic because of cost, partnership and performance, and that Replit's own tests show OpenAI's models build apps from scratch better. TechCrunch adds that a person familiar with the partnership said it is still in place, and that Replit's own late-September blog post named Anthropic's Claude models as running its coding agent.
notes: Read TechCrunch in full (it was updated to add the contrary evidence and says Replit had not yet clarified). Masad also said enterprise was about 2% of Replit's revenue last year and about 15% now, with more than half B2B; not used in the summary. Replit announced an OpenAI partnership in August 2026.
